Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ajar usually hope their child will grow to embody breath, life and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Ajar is a name deeply rooted in Hindu tradition and symbolism, as it represents the very essence of life itself. In Hindu culture, respect for life is of utmost importance, and the name Ajar serves as a constant reminder of this value. It is believed that having a name that signifies life will bestow upon the boy a long and healthy life. Moreover, naming a child Ajar would be considered a respectful homage to the god Prana, who bestows the gift of life upon all beings.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ajar holds significant spiritual significance in Hinduism. It signifies the connection between the individual soul and the divine force of life, represented by the god Prana. The name Ajar serves as a daily reminder of the divine presence and the soul's continuity with it. It is believed that the boy named Ajar will be guided through his life by the blessings of Prana, the god of breath and life. The spiritual significance of the name further strengthens the individual's bond with the divine and fosters a deep sense of reverence and respect for life itself.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Ajar is believed to originate from the Sanskrit word 'Ajara', which means 'invincible' or 'unaging'. It is believed that those named Ajar are endowed with the power to overcome obstacles and live a long, healthy, and fulfilling life.

historical_references.reference: Ajar was a famous sage and a great devotee of Lord Shiva. He is mentioned in various ancient Hindu texts including the Shiva Purana and the Skanda Purana. In the Shiva Purana, Ajar is described as a king who ruled over the city of Vidisha in central India. He is said to have attained enlightenment after worshiping Lord Shiva for years.

Ajar is also referred to in the Jain text, the Harivamsha, as a Jain Tirthankara (a spiritual teacher). He is believed to have lived around the 12th century BCE and is known for his 16 dream visions, which are considered significant in Jainism.
